questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a spanish speaking country so i could improve and use my spanish but also be able to take my academic courses in english as my spanish is not good enough for university level.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Mexico is a great destination for a semester abroad, I had an unforgettable experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: fairly easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: if you arrive on the recommended day of the university there will be university staff at the airport to help you find the right bus to cholula. the first 3 days at the university where orientation days where we got most of the information we needed

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: the orientation was good but the assistance was not. The international student coordinator was rude and not very helpful and it was difficult to change courses.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: its very easy to find off campus housing in Cholula, and its much better and cheaper than the on campus housing. The campus dorms have curfues and doesnt allow overnight visitors or alcohol.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: the easiest way to live off campus is to live with one of the housing companies in cholula. I personally lived with Cholula capital in casa Naranja and i really enjoyed it. they have several houses which you can check out on their website and they do a lot of social events and trips so its really easy to make friends. It is also a very social way to live and you will have a lot of roomies. there are also other companies such as si señor, travels life and casa leyenda which i have heard other people say great things about as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: over all the off campus housing in cholula is great most of the houses are really nice and social and have great location in walking distance to the university and the bars and resturants in the city. some of the closest friends i made during my stay was my roomies and have a social network from the begining was really nice.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: there were a lot of documents needed and it wasnt super clear what these documents where. the university requries alot of medical information which took time to get from the doctor

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: the platform for the registration process was easy to use but they had several issuses with it and so uploading the documents and getting them accepted was difficult. they extended the deadline several times because of the issues.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: there is a whatsapp group for all incoming students where there is a lot of information, but people also ask a lot of questions and it can be hard to navigate. I also emailed the international coordinator alot and she was very helpful however she quit before we arrived and the new coordinator was very rude.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the courses i wanted except of the spanish ones i applied for. when I arrived we were told we could potentially change courses and ask about avaliability. whoever when I ask about the beginner spanish courses the coordinator questioned if ihad past the spanish placement test and told me that the course was full. I found out later talking to people whohad the course that the class was only half full.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: be patient and dont be afraid to email and ask questions. the information is not great so you have to ask for a lot of additional information which is easy enough to get if you ask.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had a few different course levels some were first year courses and others third year. I would say that the general level of the courses are lower than at KU. So if you are looking to be challenged academically UDLAP might not be the place for you.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: it much more like gymnasiet, there is a lot of group projects and presentations, hand in assignments, homework that has to be done and uploaded, and attendence. the clases are small and most of the lessons are a seminar style rather than a lecture but if also depends on the teacher.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
TEORÍA POLÍTICA Y SOCIAL I
TEORÍA DE LAS RELACIONES INTERNACIONALES
DERECHOS HUMANOS
HISTORIA DE LAS RELACIONES INTERNACIONALES
COMUNICACIÓN Y GLOBALIZACIÓN

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: DERECHOS HUMANOS with Samuel Stone was an amazing course, he is a great and passionet teacher and the course covers some really interesting topics both internatinal and mexican.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: not really any

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: housing is cheap and so is eating out, grocceries are not as cheap as you might expect but still cheaper than in denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: you cant join any of the establish sports teams but you can make your own international team. The facilaties are good they have a gym and a pool and the clubs at the university make a lot of different activities that you can participate in.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there where several activities provided both by the university and the clubs, like movie nights, or womens rights talks, sports matches and lanugage groups. the university also had bigger celebartions like on independence day with activities, dance and food trucks.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: use the sports facilities and go to the football matches, and the bonfire nights with revolución violeta

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go on trips around mexico, it is very easy to get around by bus to most parts of the country and there are soo many beautiful cities and nature. I would definately recommend going to Chiapas to see the palenque ruins and San Cristobal althought it is a longer trip. Closer to cholula I recommend hiking La Malinche, its amazing or staying in a cabin close to the volcano popo that you can see form cholula.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy, it helps to know basic spanish enough to order and be polite, traffic is a bit more caotic so be careful when walking or biking.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: a good way to talk to the people in your classes is to do group projects together and go from there. most of them are very helpful and sweet and will invite you to parties and such. be good at asking for instagrams and whatsapp this a good way to make contact with the local students and show them that you are interested in getting to know them. Also inviting them to the international student events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Time and being punctual is a bit different here so dont be too stressed when meeting people or going to things on time other than class.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: people are very open, helpful and friendly

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
enjoy the city and the university and its social life
travel as much as you can during your stay
dont stress to much about the courses

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: exams nearly all fall in the same week so dont make too many plans the last week of the semester

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: just being in mexico and creating and everyday life in cholula and at the university while also getting to visit amazing places on the weekends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: keeping up with school work, not because the level is difficult but because there are a lot of assignments and deadlines to keep track of and different teachers will use different platforms.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: generally I think UDLAP is a great university and cholula is a wonderful city to live in and i would definatly recommend going

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
